messages:
nina: running into duplicates in the Java sample app when customers hit a burst of 429s during onboarding. quick sanity thread.

raphael: can you paste the minimal trace? is it the SDK sending two requests or our server reprocessing?

nina: SDK sent two. sequence:
```
client POST /v1/creates -> 429
SDK: start async token refresh
SDK: retry POST immediately (no idempotency header) -> 201
refresh completes, original path also retries -> 201
```

jo: ugh race between retry path and refresh completion. our Java SDK used to await a single refresh promise, but we recently changed to parallel refresh to reduce latency and accidentally allowed double-sends.

raphael: options: 1) reintroduce a retry gate that awaits refresh; 2) make sampleapps add X-Idempotency-Key by default; 3) SDK can offer opt-in auto-idempotency generation.

nina: for onboarding I vote for sampleapp change + docs + a lint check to flag POSTs missing idempotency. SDK change can be opt-in to avoid surprising users.

jo: agreed. also recommend conservative defaults for backoff in sampleapps: retries=3, max_backoff=8s, jitter=25%. reduces collision window for naive apps.

raphael: I'll open a small MR to gate retries on outstanding refresh and add telemetry (retry_during_refresh=true) so we can measure.

build-bot: MR opened: https://git.redwood/sdks/mr/1012 — tests queued :gear:

nina: thanks — i'll patch the Java sample app and add the README snippet showing how to set X-Idempotency-Key (UUID example). will also add the lint rule as a warning for now.

jo: once merged let's backfill an integration test that simulates 429 + stalled refresh. good catch. :+1:
